newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends 25 cts down, Brent stays near $18.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends 25 cts down, Brent stays near $18.

text.p: IPE April gas oil ended 25 cents a tonne down at $162 on Monday after slipping 50 cents near the close.

Despite modestly firmer prices, which peaked at $163 in the afternoon, gas oil remains pressured. The low of $160.75 hit last Friday was only slightly above the $159.50 which traded about a month ago and was the lowest level since last summer.

These low levels were traded despite big demand into Asia in recent months. China saw a massive 97 percent jump in year-on-year light diesel imports to 1.27 million tonnes in January and February this year.
IPE Brent was firm during late afternoon trading but was below highs earlier.
May Brent was up 35 cents a barrel at $18.03 at 1626 GMT having peaked at $18.11 soon after the NYMEX opening.
Dealers were watching to see if Brent manages to close above $18, the psychological support level through which it plunged last Friday when it dipped to nine month lows.
"The question now is whether we hold above $18," a broker said.
If we do I think we can start to see the market starting to push back up towards $18.30 on the May Brent," he added.
"The fundamentals are still the same. There is a lot of crude, we all know that dated Brent is weak and we know there's a lot of overhang in the market".
"But saying that, we've known this now for two weeks...the main question is how much of this is already discounted".
Despite gains on IPE Brent futures, the physical martket for crude oil remains depressed.
Supplies of sour crude are rising and selling Brent to the U.S. remains difficult. A physical cargo of Brent crude costs about $1 a barrel below IPE May Brent.
